name: MyScript Notes
tagline: Handwritten note-taking that converts ink to editable text on the fly, built on MyScript's own recognition engine.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The notebook shell is trivial: canvas, strokes, pages, pressure, undo, export. The product is not the notebook, it is the recognition engine, which MyScript has been building since the 1990s across dozens of languages, scripts, math, and diagrams, on device, in real time, while you are still writing. An agent can wire up Apple's PencilKit text recognition or Google's ML Kit Digital Ink and get something that reads tidy Latin print, but that is renting someone else's model, not replacing one, and accuracy on real cursive drops off a cliff. Cross-device sync is the boring part and genuinely solvable with a file in a cloud drive. The hard part stays hard: nobody one-shots a handwriting recognizer, and the good ones are not open.
coreLoopDIY: A local Android tablet notebook that captures stylus ink, stores it as vector strokes, and converts a selected block to text via on-device ML Kit Digital Ink Recognition.
requirements: Android tablet with an active stylus (S Pen or similar)
Android Studio and a willingness to debug touch vs stylus input
ML Kit Digital Ink Recognition model downloads per language
Patience with recognition accuracy on anything resembling real cursive
whatYouLose: Recognition quality: MyScript reads messy cursive and mixed scripts that ML Kit will mangle
Math, diagrams, and chemistry ink converted into structured objects rather than text
Interactive ink gestures: scratch to delete, split, join, reflow of handwritten paragraphs
Real cross-platform parity, you get one platform, not iPad and Android both
Language coverage, MyScript spans scores of languages and input scripts
moatNotes: The recognizers are trained on decades of collected handwriting samples per script, and that corpus is not something you assemble over a weekend or scrape.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the entire value is the half second between lifting your pen and seeing correct text, and that half second is twenty five years of model work. People who write by hand are usually doing it because typing breaks their thinking, which means a recognizer that is 85 percent accurate is worse than useless: they end up proofreading instead of thinking. MyScript's engine is also on device, so it works on a plane with no account and no upload, which is a big part of why the people who like it really like it. A DIY shell plus a borrowed recognizer gets you a nice ink canvas and a text button you stop pressing.
notes: The notebook is a weekend; the recognizer is not. The moat is decades of collected handwriting data and the on-device models trained on it.
prompt:
Build a local-first handwriting notebook for Android tablets. Native Android, Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, minSdk 26. No backend, no accounts, no telemetry.

In scope:
- A notebook list screen: create, rename, delete notebooks. Each notebook has ordered pages.
- A page editor with a full-screen ink canvas. Capture MotionEvent stylus input including pressure and tilt; render strokes as smoothed polylines with pressure-varying width. Treat finger input as pan/zoom, stylus as ink. Add a toggle so finger can also draw.
- Tools: pen (3 widths, 6 colors), eraser (stroke-level erase, not pixel), lasso select, undo/redo with a real command stack.
- Store strokes as vectors in Room: stroke id, page id, tool, color, width, and a list of timestamped x/y/pressure points. Never store bitmaps as the source of truth.
- Text conversion: integrate Google ML Kit Digital Ink Recognition (on-device). Let the user lasso a region or convert a whole page, feed the selected strokes as an Ink object, and show the recognized text in a bottom sheet with a Copy button and an "insert as text block" option that replaces the strokes with a typed paragraph on the page. Handle model download per language with visible progress; default to en-US, allow picking from the available language list in settings.
- Export: a page or notebook to PDF (vector where possible) and to plain .txt for whatever was converted.
- Backup: export/import the whole database plus strokes as a single .zip to a user-picked SAF location.

Out of scope, do not build: cloud sync, a server, iPad or web clients, math recognition, diagram beautification, OCR of imported photos, collaboration, auth.

Rules: no network calls except the ML Kit model download. No secrets needed; if you add any config, put it in .env style local.properties and gitignore it. Write a README that states plainly that recognition accuracy depends entirely on the ML Kit model and will be noticeably worse than commercial engines on cursive. Include a seed script that generates one sample notebook so the app is not empty on first run.
